heading: INT. PROUTY COTTAGE - PARLOR - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. PROUTY COTTAGE - PARLOR - LATE AFTERNOON
A low-ceilinged room.
A mantel crowded with china figurines.
A shawl on the arm of a chair.
A grandfather's walking stick leaning by the door.
Rain taps the windows.
ELEANOR PROUTY, 60s, in a gray cardigan, sits in the straight-backed chair with her hands folded.
GERALD, 60s, her brother-in-law, stands at the window with his back to her.
CONSTABLE IDRIS, 30s, young and awkward, perches on the edge of the settee with a notebook on his knee.
Mrs. Prouty. I'm sorry to trouble you.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: It's no trouble.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: I only have a few questions.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Of course.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: Gerald does not turn.
His hand rests on the curtain.
When did you last see your husband?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Tuesday morning. At breakfast.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: And he went to the allotment?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: He always goes to the allotment.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: Did he mention anyone?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: No.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: Idris writes.
The pen scratches in the silence.
A clock chimes the quarter hour.
Was he in good spirits?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: He was quiet.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: Gerald lets the curtain fall.
Henry was always quiet.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Mr. Prouty, you live next door?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Forty years.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: And you didn't see him Tuesday?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: I saw him walk past. Around nine.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Which direction?
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Toward the river.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Eleanor looks down at her hands.
She turns her wedding ring a single quarter turn.
The allotment is the other way.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Nobody speaks.
Idris closes the notebook.
Gerald crosses to the mantel and straightens a china shepherdess that did not need straightening.
Perhaps he went for a walk.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Perhaps.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Would you like tea, Constable?
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: That would be kind.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: She rises and goes to the kitchen.
Gerald watches her go.
When the kettle clatters in the other room, he turns to Idris with an expression that is almost relief.
She has not slept since Tuesday.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: No. I should think not.
units.name: IDRIS

units.text: Idris tucks the notebook into his pocket.
He glances at the walking stick by the door.
It is wet.
Rain, perhaps.
Or river.
